policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: The readings differ only in the two articles of τῶν ὑδάτων τῶν, and ASV 'upon many waters' gives neither of them a separate realization.

The three readings differ only in the form of the participle and in one article; ASV 'full of names of blasphemy' shows neither, and its note 'Or, names full of blasphemy' offers a construal rather than a text.
The variant is the gender of the participle agreeing with θηρίον; ASV 'having seven heads and ten horns' is identical under ἔχων and ἔχον.
ASV 'and decked with gold' renders the connective, and it renders every other καί of the verse as 'and', so the reading without it is not the text behind this clause.
χρυσίῳ and χρυσῷ are alternative forms of the same noun, both rendered 'gold'; ASV's note 'Greek gilded' belongs to κεχρυσωμένη, not to this word.
ASV joins the two blood phrases with a conjunction — 'of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs' — so the asyndetic reading is not the text it rendered.
ASV 'and to go into perdition' renders the infinitive ὑπάγειν, and its note 'Some ancient authorities read and he goeth' maps the indicative ὑπάγει as the reading it did not follow.
Passive θαυμασθήσονται and middle θαυμάσονται are both future forms of θαυμάζω rendered 'shall wonder'; ASV marks no difference of voice here.
ASV 'they whose name hath not been written' is singular, so τὸ ὄνομα rather than the plural τὰ ὀνόματα is the text it rendered.
ASV 'when they behold the beast, how that he was' keeps τὸ θηρίον outside the ὅτι clause and leaves a pronoun inside it, which is the base order and not RP's ὅτι ἦν τὸ θηρίον.
ASV 'The seven heads are seven mountains' must set the copula before its predicate in English, so ἑπτά εἰσιν and εἰσιν ἑπτὰ are indistinguishable.
ASV 'he must continue a little while' fixes the English order of subject and verb, so it does not report whether αὐτόν stood before or after δεῖ.
ASV 'is himself also an eighth' renders the intensive αὐτός; οὗτος would give 'this one' or a plain 'he'.
ASV 'These have one mind' puts verb before object as English requires, so γνώμην ἔχουσιν and ἔχουσιν γνώμην are indistinguishable.
The variant is the article alone, and ASV 'their power and authority' carries one possessive across both nouns whether or not the Greek repeats τὴν.
ASV 'shall make her desolate and naked' governs both adjectives with a single verb, so RP's repeated ποιήσουσιν αὐτήν is not the text it rendered.
ASV 'to come to one mind' fixes the English order of numeral and noun, so μίαν γνώμην and γνώμην μίαν are indistinguishable.
Future indicative τελεσθήσονται and aorist subjunctive τελεσθῶσιν after ἄχρι are both rendered 'until the words of God should be accomplished'.
